newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council rejects Giuliani "Superstore" proposal.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council rejects Giuliani "Superstore" proposal.

text.p: The New York City Council on Wednesday rejected Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's plan to allow so-called superstores of up to 200,000 square feet to be built in areas zoned for manufacturing.
City Council Speaker Peter vallone, a Democrat, said the council would try to develop its own plan.
The 47-to-1 vote came after months of contention between the mayor and council over plans to permit "as of right" construction of the "big box" stores.
Giuliani, a Republican, said the zoning change was needed because many New Yorkers are shopping in the suburbs and because larger super markets would provide food more cheaply in the inner city.
Council members said Guiliani's plan prevented community review of large developments.
